claims.text: The DGAC established CEFAA (Comité de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos) on 3 October 1997.

On 18 October 2021, by Resolución Exenta N° 04/3/0113/1385, CEFAA was reorganised as SEFAA (Sección de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos) and placed under the Communications Subdepartment of the DGAC.

SEFAA investigates reports using declared scientific method with emphasis on audiovisual evidence, accepts public case submissions through an official reporting system, and maintains a public database of resolved cases organised by year.

Chile's twenty-nine-year run of an open civil-aviation UAP office, publishing analyses and releasing military-origin footage, shifts the burden of proof onto the party claiming that public handling of UAP data would cause unacceptable harm. Reasoning: the predicted harms did not materialise in a state with comparable air-sovereignty concerns.

connections.note: Chile's Direccion General de Aeronautica Civil dates CEFAA's establishment to 3 October 1997 and hosts it: after the 2021 reorganisation the successor body SEFAA 'operates within the General Directorate of Civil Aeronautics', as Canada's Sky Canada report independently describes it. General Ricardo Bermudez Sanhueza, who took over the Escuela Tecnica Aeronautica in 1997, also took the direction of the committee and served until 2016.

Recommendation 13 tells the proposed Canadian lead organization to establish partnerships with SEFAA (Chile) among others.

desc: The Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil is Chile's civil aviation authority, and it is the only such body in the hemisphere to have operated a permanent, publicly acknowledged office for the study of anomalous aerial phenomena for nearly three decades. On 3 October 1997 the DGAC created the Comité de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (CEFAA); on 18 October 2021 it reorganised that committee by Resolución Exenta N° 04/3/0113/1385 into the Sección de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos (SEFAA), placing it under the DGAC's Communications Subdepartment. SEFAA takes case submissions from the public through an official reporting channel, analyses them by declared scientific method with emphasis on audiovisual evidence, and publishes a case database organised by year - the analyses go out, not just the intake. Under General Ricardo Bermúdez, who directed CEFAA from 1997 to 2016, the office released military sensor footage and published its own conclusions on cases it could not resolve. Chile matters to this board as a control case: a state with real air-defence equities ran an open UAP office for twenty-nine years and released classified-origin footage without the consequences the American concealment argument depends on, and Canada's Chief Science Advisor identified it in June 2025 as one of only three national models worth copying alongside AARO and France's GEIPAN.
